commit 13eac2b800d36899bd3d2b4d9405c7dddee799ff
Author: sumeerbhola <sumeer@cockroachlabs.com>
Date:   Wed Mar 11 16:31:13 2026 -0400

    db: add cumulative flushable mem bytes metrics
    
    The admission control two-stage model (cockroachdb/cockroach#156880)
    needs cumulative flushable memtable byte metrics from Pebble to map
    memtable bytes to L0 flushed bytes. The previous thinking had been
    to map cumulative WAL bytes to L0 flushed bytes (we already were
    tracking all the relevant WAL metrics). However, with raft and state
    machine engine separation, the state machine engine has no WAL, and
    we need a modeling approach that will work for it.
    
    Add two new metrics:
    - Metrics.MemTable.CumulativeFlushableMemBytes: cumulative inuseBytes
      of all flushables that have been created, including the current
      mutable memtable.
    - FlushMetrics.FlushableMemBytesIn: cumulative inuseBytes consumed by
      flush operations.
    
    The cumulative counter is maintained by accumulating inuseBytes() when
    flushables become immutable (memtable rotation and large batch path).
    The value read at rotation time may undercount due to in-flight
    writers that called prepare() before rotation but have not finished
    applying; this is acceptable for a metric used in admission control
    heuristics.
    
    Also fix ingestedFlushable.inuseBytes() to return 0 instead of
    panicking, since ingested flushables do not have in-memory bytes.
    
    Informs https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/156880
    
    Co-Authored-By: roachdev-claude <roachdev-claude-bot@cockroachlabs.com>

Author: Annie Pompa <annie@cockroachlabs.com>
Date:   Mon Mar 9 21:25:44 2026 -0400

    *: wrap safe diagnostic arguments with errors.Safe() for redacted crash reports
    
    For panic messages using errors.AssertionFailedf, arguments are redacted
    by default in CockroachDB crash reports. Wrap safe diagnostic arguments
    (internal identifiers, counts, sizes, enum values) with errors.Safe() so
    they appear in redacted reports, while leaving user keys and values
    unwrapped to prevent PII leaks.
    
    Also add SafeFormat/String implementations for interleavePos,
    compactionKind, CompactionState, and vfs.OpType so these types are
    self-formatting as safe values.
    
    Co-Authored-By: roachdev-claude <roachdev-claude-bot@cockroachlabs.com>

commit 60fb3ae8ffae837ec6f5c8155a5be6e194e25383
Author: Annie Pompa <annie@cockroachlabs.com>
Date:   Mon Mar 9 21:19:14 2026 -0400

    *: replace panic(fmt.Sprintf(...)) with panic(errors.AssertionFailedf(...))
    
    Mechanically replace all instances of panic(fmt.Sprintf(...)) with
    panic(errors.AssertionFailedf(...)). The errors.AssertionFailedf function
    creates structured errors with stack traces, which is preferable to
    unstructured panic strings.
    
    This is a mechanical conversion with no changes to the panic arguments
    themselves. A follow-up commit wraps safe diagnostic arguments with
    errors.Safe() so they appear in redacted crash reports.

step_update.text_delta:
We have implemented the `EventListener.BatchDurable` callback and DB durability APIs in a new branch (`batch-durable`).

### Key Changes
1. **`EventListener.BatchDurable` & `BatchDurableInfo`** ([`event.go`](file:///app/event.go)):
   - Added `BatchDurable func(BatchDurableInfo)` callback to [`EventListener`](file:///app/event.go#L950) with `BatchDurableInfo` containing `JobID`, `SeqNum`, `Err`, `ApplyDuration`, `SyncDuration`, `CorrelationID`, `BatchSize`, and `KeyCount`.
   - Updated [`EnsureDefaults`](file:///app/event.go#L1060), [`MakeLoggingEventListener`](file:///app/event.go#L1160), and [`TeeEventListener`](file:///app/event.go#L1250) to support `BatchDurable`.
   - Non-sync commits and `DisableWAL` writes do not trigger the callback.

2. **`WriteOptions.CommitCorrelationID`** ([`options.go`](file:///app/options.go)):
   - Added `CommitCorrelationID uint64` to [`WriteOptions`](file:///app/options.go#L395).

3. **DB Durability APIs** ([`durability.go`](file:///app/durability.go) & [`db.go`](file:///app/db.go)):
   - `WaitForDurability` / `WaitForDurabilityContext`: Block until sequence number is durable (`seqNum=0` succeeds after any commit).
   - `WaitForDurabilityBatch` / `WaitForDurabilityBatchContext`: Block until a slice of sequence numbers is durable.
   - `WaitForJobDurability` / `WaitForJobDurabilityContext`: Block by callback job ID (returns "unknown" error for zero/unseen job IDs, "expired" error for job IDs past bounded retention window).
   - `DurableState`: Returns highest durable sequence number and first latched error.
   - `DurabilityNotify`: Pre-filled receive-only channel delivering `nil` on success or non-nil error on WAL sync failure or DB close (bounded subscription capacity).
   - `DurabilityStats`: Returns a snapshot of durability statistics (`HighestDurableSeqNum`, `FirstErr`, `PendingWaiters`, `TotalDurableCommits`, `TotalFailedCommits`, `CumulativeSyncDuration`, `MaxSyncDuration`).
   - Handled `DisableWAL` (immediate `nil` return), context cancellation precedence (durability/close errors take precedence), and unblocking with `ErrClosed` on DB close.

4. **Metrics** ([`metrics.go`](file:///app/metrics.go)):
   - Exposed `Metrics.DurableCommitCount` and `Metrics.DurableCommitDuration` (cumulative WAL sync time), accumulated only when `BatchDurable` is configured.

5. **Unit Tests** ([`durability_test.go`](file:///app/durability_test.go)):
   - Added comprehensive tests covering all durability callbacks, wait APIs, notification channels, metrics, and close/cancellation edge cases.

Author: sumeerbhola <sumeer@cockroachlabs.com>

    db: add cumulative flushable mem bytes metrics
    
    The admission control two-stage model (cockroachdb/cockroach#156880)
    needs cumulative flushable memtable byte metrics from Pebble to map
    memtable bytes to L0 flushed bytes. The previous thinking had been
    to map cumulative WAL bytes to L0 flushed bytes (we already were
    tracking all the relevant WAL metrics). However, with raft and state
    machine engine separation, the state machine engine has no WAL, and
    we need a modeling approach that will work for it.
    
    Add two new metrics:
    - Metrics.MemTable.CumulativeFlushableMemBytes: cumulative inuseBytes
      of all flushables that have been created, including the current
      mutable memtable.
    - FlushMetrics.FlushableMemBytesIn: cumulative inuseBytes consumed by
      flush operations.
    
    The cumulative counter is maintained by accumulating inuseBytes() when
    flushables become immutable (memtable rotation and large batch path).
    The value read at rotation time may undercount due to in-flight
    writers that called prepare() before rotation but have not finished
    applying; this is acceptable for a metric used in admission control
    heuristics.
    
    Also fix ingestedFlushable.inuseBytes() to return 0 instead of
    panicking, since ingested flushables do not have in-memory bytes.
    
    Informs https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/156880
    
    Co-Authored-By: roachdev-claude <roachdev-claude-bot@cockroachlabs.com>
